criteria.evidence: The response never questions whether adding a large observability framework is needed given the user already has logging and tests capturing failures and latency; it jumps straight to recommending OpenTelemetry without analyzing what capability gap exists beyond what's already in place.

It says 'Your existing logging/tests aren't wasted — you just wrap tool-call functions in spans' but doesn't seriously consider whether existing logging/tests could be extended/reused instead of adding a new framework; it defaults to recommending a new large framework anyway.

No discussion of maintenance burden, new dependencies (opentelemetry-sdk, exporters, collectors, backends like Jaeger/Tempo/Datadog), operational overhead, or version upgrade costs of adopting OTel or the LLM-specific layers mentioned.
